purpose: Whole-journey product and accessibility acceptance; not component-unit-test duplication or achieved usability evidence.

measurement_rules.activation: Click, tap or equivalent command activation; include file chooser and confirmations.
measurement_rules.elapsed_time: Report full elapsed time alongside the stated active-software budget and separately observed components.
measurement_rules.cohorts: Record novice/experienced and access-need groups, unaided/assisted completion, raw counts, median/spread and uncertainty; formative samples are not population qualification.
measurement_rules.telemetry: Collect workflow state, action category, duration and outcome without copying participant answers, raw physiology, video/audio or identity into UX telemetry.
measurement_rules.accessibility: Automated scans supplement observed keyboard/screen-reader/reflow tasks; they do not substitute for them.
measurement_rules.zero_targets: A zero-defect target is an acceptance requirement for the tested journey, not evidence that all configurations are error-free.

journeys.name: First report from a prepared sample
preconditions: Fictional sample with prepared materials and recordings; installed environment
actions: Open sample
Follow the main action through preparation and results
Explain the report and download it
acceptance: Sample origin stays visible and never increases real participant counts
No mandatory scientific configuration or empty review confirmation
User explains comparison, measure, usable sample and uncertainty
evidence: Observed action log including file dialogs

journeys.name: Author the complete multimodal flagship
journeys.actor: Novice with prepared assets and saved station
preconditions: Supported eye/EEG/EDA profiles; named BIAT and physical AAT profiles
actions: Choose prepared flagship recipe
Add control/test assets and semantic AOIs
Inspect phase preview and selected measure cards
Prepare participant flow
acceptance: Control image, physiological baseline, practice, passive viewing and question periods remain distinct
Recipe specifies allocation and task-block order/counterbalancing
Capture uses the current compiled questionnaire/protocol hash; subsequent edits create a new revision
Every selected measure states phases and expected outputs
evidence: Rendered phase list and frozen run bundle
User explanation of control versus baseline

journeys.name: Linked questionnaire branching and correction
preconditions: Repeated A/B exposures, post-exposure liking, conditional follow-up and required item
actions: Preview both order variants
Change a branch-driving answer
Submit an incomplete required item then correct it
Inspect linked report
acceptance: Each answer refers to the actual presentation and question revision
Untouched, skipped, not shown and declined remain distinct
Current hidden dependent answers follow policy while append-only history survives
Error summary links/focuses the field; preview exit restores launcher

journeys.name: Every capability fits shared cards and readiness
preconditions: Representative supported, import-only, unavailable and optional profiles across every surface in surface_coverage
actions: Add and remove measures
Reuse one source across several measures
Resolve one readiness action
Open one extension's import or profile route
acceptance: All 50 capability IDs have a user-facing surface mapping
No measure creates an empty or disconnected dashboard
One readiness summary names required blockers and optional consequences
Completing setup restores focus to the originating card; device mapping is reused

journeys.name: Simultaneous eye, EEG and EDA viewing
preconditions: Approved named station profile and configured recipe; synthetic fixture route for software checks
actions: Start participant
Complete baseline and counterbalanced viewing with linked questions
Open synchronized timeline
Inspect modality results
acceptance: One run links all streams to realized exposure IDs and phase events
Planned/requested times remain distinct from observed onset evidence
One timeline/table shows signal coverage and clock uncertainty
Passive-viewing analysis excludes question and motor periods according to recipe
journeys.qualification_note: Synthetic software execution does not qualify a physical station.

journeys.name: Sequential BIAT and physical AAT inside the same study
preconditions: Named BIAT procedure and supported physical AAT input; block-order plan
actions: Follow separate instructions and practice
Complete scored BIAT and AAT blocks
Inspect study report
acceptance: Practice and scored trials have separate inclusion rules
BIAT retains first and final-correct timing; AAT retains neutral state and movement trace
Each block uses its own score, direction, exclusions and response demands
Continuous physiological recording is phase-linked; movement data are not treated as passive viewing
evidence: Task event traces with block lineage

journeys.name: Optional webcam and microphone with shared capture
preconditions: Selected camera/microphone routes and explicit capture/provider choices
actions: Select facial outputs and optional webcam gaze or camera physiology
Review capture choices
Grant or decline permissions
Inspect available outputs
acceptance: One camera capture supplies permitted dependent models without competing camera sessions
Independent webcam gaze calibration/validation has an actionable step
Declined optional camera/microphone preserves permitted sensor and questionnaire routes
No-face, occlusion and unvoiced support do not become zero scores
Provider destination and native model/output identity are inspectable

journeys.name: Sensor loss without losing the study
preconditions: Active multimodal run; explicit optional and required stream-loss policies
actions: Encounter seeded optional EDA disconnect
Read affected-data message and repair or continue
Repeat with a required-signal-loss scenario
acceptance: Other valid streams and responses remain stored and eligible
Optional loss follows frozen continue policy; required loss invokes declared stop/pause boundary
Recovery creates a segment/gap rather than fabricated continuity
Operator identifies affected outcomes and a permitted next action

journeys.name: Interrupted participant trial and durable recovery
preconditions: Task interruption policy; persistence acknowledgement available
actions: Reload or lose focus during a timed trial
Reopen session
Choose the protocol-permitted recovery
acceptance: UI names the last durably saved boundary and interrupted presentation
Retry/restart has a new attempt/presentation identity; old data remain auditable
No duplicate allocation, answer or quietly resumed timed trial
Focus moves to recovery heading and then the chosen action

journeys.name: Import several modalities with one repair
preconditions: Eye/physiology/event files with one deliberately ambiguous unit or clock
actions: Add files in one import action
Resolve the contextual mapping issue
Inspect automatic preparation and linked outcomes
acceptance: Original bytes remain retained with provenance
Ambiguous units/clocks are explained beside concrete source values and affected measures
Unambiguous streams progress without guessing or row-number alignment
Mapping correction affects only its dependent outputs

journeys.name: Analysis cancellation and restart
preconditions: At least two modality jobs and an older report
actions: Cancel or encounter a worker failure
Continue other work
Retry the failed job
Reopen results
acceptance: Progress reports real stage/units; indeterminate work has no invented percentage
Unaffected jobs/results remain available
Expired or cancelled attempts cannot publish stale success
Retry resumes valid dependencies and preserves previous report revision
Status announcements do not steal focus

journeys.name: Correct an automated AOI and understand its effect
preconditions: Plausible wrong AOI proposal plus a gaze-gap case
actions: Inspect grouped exception
Correct geometry using pointer or numeric/keyboard equivalent
Preview affected results
Apply and optionally undo
acceptance: Proposed versus accepted geometry is distinguishable
Correction has revision, provenance and downstream impact
First-fixation nonhits follow declared observability policy when gaps could hide a hit
Focus returns to reviewed row or next exception; unrelated outcomes remain intact
evidence: Before/after metric agreement with declared reference

journeys.name: Explain and export one multimodal report
preconditions: Completed cohort with at least one partially missing modality
actions: Read primary comparison and supporting outcomes
Open one evidence detail
Download accessible report and reproducible bundle
Answer four comprehension questions
acceptance: Attention, explicit liking, physiology and task scores remain distinguishable
Valid participant/stimulus support and uncertainty accompany every outcome
Missing one modality does not silently remove other usable outcomes
Recipient identifies comparison, operational measure, usable coverage and uncertainty
evidence: Blinded recipient responses with raw counts and assistance

journeys.name: Keyboard-only whole-study completion
preconditions: Declared desktop browser matrix; supported prepared fixture
actions: Author and reorder flow without dragging
Edit one AOI numerically
Handle validation and readiness
Navigate timeline and export report
acceptance: No pointer-only step or keyboard trap
Focus is visible and follows logical order
Dialogs restore focus; error summaries link to fields
Tables and list views provide equivalent actions and information

journeys.name: Screen-reader navigation and live status
journeys.actor: Researcher using a declared screen reader/browser pairing
preconditions: Declared tested pairing, such as NVDA with a supported Windows browser
actions: Navigate landmarks/cards
Correct a questionnaire error
Observe acquisition status and seeded failure
Read result table and export
acceptance: Names, roles, values and relationships are understandable
Polite save/progress messages do not repeat at sample rate
Critical required-stop announcement is concise and actionable
Dynamic updates preserve current reading/focus position
Visual timeline and charts have meaningful equivalent tables

journeys.name: Reflow, zoom and reduced motion
journeys.actor: Researcher with low vision or motion sensitivity
preconditions: 320 CSS pixel viewport or 400% zoom; reduced-motion preference
actions: Use every stage at narrow/reflow layout
Complete a matrix item through its alternative
Inspect a wide scientific table
Run participant preview with motion-sensitive requirements
acceptance: Controls, errors and main action remain reachable without whole-page horizontal scrolling
Wide tables scroll within labelled regions; plots have tables
Decorative movement respects preference
Scientific stimulus motion/timing is unchanged unless a separate accommodation profile is selected

journeys.name: Next participant, collection finish and reuse
preconditions: Saved station and completed first participant; eligible cohort
actions: Start next participant
Finish collection explicitly
Download frozen report
Create a new study from the pinned recipe
acceptance: New participant inherits station setup, not prior answers or run identity
Participant finish and collection finish are visibly distinct
Finalization freezes cohort and triggers the agreed report without analysis reconfiguration
Reopening or reusing preserves the original report and creates new study/revision identity

journeys.name: Accessible task accommodation without hidden method changes
journeys.actor: Participant and researcher selecting an accommodation
preconditions: Participant need changes input, presentation, instruction or timing demands
actions: Open accessible alternatives
Select a supported accommodation profile or an appropriate alternative task
Preview the actual participant experience
Inspect report grouping
acceptance: Accommodation has a clear path with readable explanation
No quiet conversion of physical AAT to keyboard AAT or timed task to untimed equivalent
Input/display/timing and profile revision are retained
Analysis eligibility/grouping follows the selected profile while authoring/reporting remain accessible

journeys.name: Find and reopen historical research
preconditions: Several active and archived studies in different projects; a preserved final report and linked dataset
actions: Restart Brohn
Find the archived study using search and project/date/status filters
Open its report and linked dataset
Restore the study to the active library
acceptance: The library restores from durable metadata independently of a prior browser session
Search and permissions expose the permitted study, revision, report and data lineage
Archiving or restoring library visibility does not delete data, reopen recruitment or change the final report
The overview offers the actual next action and a direct Clone this design action
evidence: Preserved report hashes and deployment state

journeys.name: Curate and reuse a historical dataset
preconditions: A multi-file multimodal dataset with provenance and a second permitted study
actions: Import and inspect detected metadata
Repair an ambiguous mapping
Attach a fixed dataset version to two analyses
Inspect source files and both study links
acceptance: Dataset identity, original files, units, clocks, source rights and processing lineage remain discoverable
Ambiguous metadata becomes a repair task rather than an inferred silent conversion
Duplicate byte imports can reuse authorized content-addressed storage while retaining distinct import provenance
Attaching a dataset does not create new participants, observations or unrestricted cross-project access
Both analyses retain their selected immutable dataset versions

journeys.name: Clone a study design from library, overview or archive
journeys.actor: Researcher preparing a replication or new cohort
preconditions: An authorized source study with design, collected data and a published report; an authorized destination
actions: Select the source draft or published revision and Clone this design
Review the compact copy summary and destination/name
Create the new draft and inspect its readiness
acceptance: Clone is reachable from Library, Overview and Archive with equivalent keyboard actions
Design-only default copies permitted stimuli, design AOIs, conditions, question/recipe definitions and timing settings with complete new-ID reference remapping

Participant/contact/consent-response records, observations, answers, results, run-specific exclusions, assignments, filled quotas, invites, deployment links, secrets and station calibration do not copy
Design seeds may preserve schedule semantics while allocation and run state are fresh; approved shared asset bytes remain content-addressed with authorized references
Cross-project permissions and reuse scope are checked again on commit; source roles and links are not inherited
Original design, data and reports remain unchanged; reanalysis of an existing dataset is a distinct action
evidence: Observed clone task from all three entry points
Source-to-destination entity map and allowlist fixture
Cross-project restriction fixture and unchanged source hashes

journeys.name: Save and reuse versioned templates and assets
journeys.actor: Researcher or tutor curating reusable materials
preconditions: A reusable design with questionnaire logic, controls and design AOIs; one running deployment using a pinned revision
actions: Save an authorized design as a named template
Create a new study from the pinned template
Replace a stimulus or questionnaire revision
Inspect affected requirements and publish a later template revision
acceptance: Template reuse follows the design-only allowlist and preserves source citations and permitted lineage
Asset changes show affected AOIs, branches, scoring and readiness; no missing stimulus is silently substituted
The new study has its own editable identities while preserving valid references and recipe settings
An upstream template or asset update never changes an already pinned deployment or historical report
A required unavailable model or asset appears as a named dependency with a repair path

journeys.name: Pilot, publish and serve a participant study
preconditions: A compiled protocol and declared supported lab, supervised LAN or hosted browser route
actions: Complete the required preview and pilot
Inspect deployment readiness and publish the selected revision
Open its URL or QR destination in a fresh supported participant browser
Pause or revoke the deployment and revisit the link
acceptance: The delivery profile declares its actual reachable endpoint; a loopback address is never represented as a public participant link
Participant renderer and assets use the published immutable revision; researcher edits remain separate drafts
Preview and pilot data do not consume live allocation or enter live sample counts
Hosted routes require authenticated researcher controls, project isolation and HTTPS deployment before being offered as ready
Failed publication, closed, paused, revoked and unsupported-profile destinations show useful states without exposing researcher records
URL and QR destinations are equivalent and retain a keyboard-readable link
evidence: Fresh-browser lab and declared hosted-profile journeys

journeys.name: Participant consent, eligibility and accessible entry
preconditions: A published protocol with entry requirements, versioned consent text and optional media policy
actions: Open the participant link
Choose an available language and supported access profile
Complete required browser/input/device checks and consent
Follow eligible, declined-media or screened-out route
acceptance: Consent response links to the exact text/version and declared data destinations before permitted capture begins
Optional camera or microphone refusal preserves allowed non-media routes; required capability failure explains the applicable alternative or end state
Consent refusal, ineligibility, unanswered and participant withdrawal remain distinct outcomes
Question wording, language, access accommodation and changed input/timing profiles remain versioned
Participant-facing entry does not require a researcher account unless the selected enrollment policy explicitly requires participant authentication
evidence: Observed participant entry including keyboard and assistive-technology routes
Eligibility and optional-media branch truth tables

journeys.name: Invitations, quotas and concurrent participant starts
preconditions: A declared invitation/repeat policy and quota with one remaining place; two concurrent eligible entrants
actions: Create a scoped invitation or permitted open-link deployment
Attempt concurrent starts
Retry a lost reservation reply and expire an abandoned reservation
Revisit with a reused or revoked invitation
acceptance: Only one entrant reserves the final place; allocation and quota accounting are transactional and idempotent
Reservation expiry and completed/withdrawn/interrupted outcomes update quota counts according to the declared policy
Revoked or already-used invitations follow explicit rules without leaking study contents
Invitation/contact identity stays separate from response and analysis identifiers
Anonymous links state the limits of duplicate detection; no unsupported claim of perfect repeat prevention or hidden invasive fingerprinting

journeys.name: Resume participation and return for a later session
preconditions: A repeated-session protocol with an explicit recovery boundary and an interrupted prior session
actions: Return through the permitted resume route
Inspect the saved boundary and recover according to the profile
Return for the next scheduled session
Start another participant on the same lab machine
acceptance: Enrollment links repeated sessions while each new run, attempt and realized presentation has the required distinct identity
Recovery records the interrupted interval and never silently replays a timed trial as its original presentation
Only the declared checkpoint can resume; expired or unsupported recovery offers a truthful end or restart route
The next person receives no prior participant answers, enrollment secrets or residual capture state
Session windows and missed/late sessions remain distinguishable from completed observations
evidence: Observed returning-participant and station handoff tasks

journeys.name: Finish, withdraw and return to a recruitment destination
preconditions: Protocol-defined completion, withdrawal, screen-out and quota-full endings; an optional approved recruitment return destination
actions: Exercise each ending route
Inspect debrief and data persistence status
Follow the configured return link when applicable
Retry after delayed upload acknowledgment
acceptance: Completed, withdrawn, screened-out, quota-full and interrupted endings have distinct recorded reasons and appropriate visible messages
Participant task completion and locally or remotely durable data receipt remain separate; pending transfers never appear as verified receipt
Debrief and participant contact/withdrawal instructions match the published protocol
Configured return destinations receive only approved opaque identifiers and status fields; browser input cannot select arbitrary redirect destinations
Repeating the ending or upload acknowledgment does not duplicate completion, enrollment or data
evidence: Participant-facing ending snapshots and keyboard task

journeys.name: Monitor, pause, close and finalize collection
preconditions: An open collection window with active sessions, one pending upload and a prior provisional report
actions: Inspect participant and persistence counts
Pause recruitment
Close collection under the declared active-session policy
Resolve outstanding dependencies and finalize
Reopen through a new collection window if permitted
acceptance: Pause prevents new enrollment without silently terminating already active sessions
Close names its effect on current participants, pending uploads and eligibility rather than treating every terminal run as complete
Finalization freezes a cohort and agreed analysis snapshot after declared prerequisites; unresolved data permit only explicitly provisional output
The stopping rule and any amendment remain attributed and visible; outcome-driven changes are not hidden
Reopening creates a new collection window and report snapshot while preserving the previous final cohort and conclusion

journeys.name: Reanalyse a historical dataset without recollecting
preconditions: An immutable dataset and preserved report with known AOI, mask and method versions
actions: Choose Reanalyse existing data
Inspect and change an allowed AOI, mask or method revision
Review affected outcomes and run the new analysis
Compare original and revised reports
acceptance: Reanalysis creates a new analysis identity over explicitly selected existing observations without cloning participants or starting collection
Changes show their parameter, eligibility and descendant impact before results are promoted
Original raw files, prior review decisions and final report remain retrievable
The comparison labels changed cohort/support, method and assumptions; unlike estimates are not presented as an unexplained numerical improvement
evidence: Independent expected invalidation and comparison fixture

journeys.name: Collaborate and share a revocable frozen report
preconditions: A supported shared deployment, two editors, a scoped reviewer and a frozen report
actions: Grant the reviewer appropriate project or report access
Edit the same question from two clients and resolve the conflict
Share a named report snapshot with a selected audience
Collect another participant and then revoke the share
acceptance: Server authorization enforces project roles and object-level access; navigation visibility alone is insufficient
Concurrent edits retain both submitted drafts and show an attributed resolution rather than silently overwriting one
Comments remain attached to the specific question, AOI or revision reviewed
Recipient sees the declared immutable snapshot and only permitted included content; later responses do not alter it
Revocation prevents future access and leaves an auditable grant record; it does not claim to recall previously downloaded copies
Expired/revoked links disclose no study details and provide an accessible status
evidence: Snapshot hashes and share grant/revocation audit

journeys.name: Export and import a portable study design
journeys.actor: Researcher moving a design into a fresh workspace
preconditions: A design with nested survey logic, repeated stimuli, control/baseline phases, scoring keys and design AOIs; a clean supported destination workspace
actions: Review design contents and dependencies
Export a versioned .brohn-study.zip
Import through choose file, review and create
Resolve permitted missing dependencies and compare behavior against independent expected fixtures
acceptance: The package contains only permitted design assets and declarative definitions with manifest versions, hashes, sizes and attribution; no collected data, credentials, live links or private paths
All imported entity IDs and references are remapped consistently; original IDs remain authorized provenance only
Independent fixtures confirm graph reachability, branch truth tables, controls, timing, seeds, scoring keys, AOIs and recipe settings rather than relying solely on exporter/importer agreement
Missing redistributable rights retain a named dependency instead of silently packaging or replacing an asset; unsupported capabilities create a labelled draft with repair tasks
The imported study has fresh allocation and deployment state, never starts collection and cannot accidentally resolve an old ID to an unrelated local entity
Name collisions and repeated package hashes offer explicit new-copy or open-existing choices without overwriting another study
evidence: Independent expected protocol and questionnaire fixtures including non-ASCII names
ID/reference mapping and design-only allowlist checks
Observed keyboard export/import and dependency-repair task

journeys.name: Reject unsafe or incompatible design packages atomically
journeys.actor: Researcher importing an invalid or incomplete package
preconditions: Fixtures with an unmigratable schema, an unexpectedly missing declared file, tampered content, escaping paths, archive expansion/size excess and disallowed executable content
actions: Attempt each invalid import
Inspect the actionable validation result and cancel or retry
Interrupt validation or exhaust available storage
Inspect the destination library and network/process evidence
acceptance: Incompatible structural schemas, missing declared bundled files, hash mismatch, path traversal and configured resource-limit violations fail before a visible study is committed
Legitimately declared external or unavailable capability dependencies remain distinct from corrupt packages and can create only a labelled draft under the portable contract
Bounded quarantine validates actual streamed sizes, hashes, entry types and resolved paths; absolute/UNC/drive paths, links, collisions and unsupported active content cannot escape or execute
Import never automatically evaluates uploaded code, installs packages, runs models or fetches network assets
Cancellation, disk failure, permission loss and process interruption leave no visible partial study; staged bytes are reconciled safely and retry is idempotent
Error output names the violated condition and preserves unrelated studies and shared objects
evidence: Adversarial ZIP and schema fixtures with expected failures

journeys.name: Restore and relocate a whole workspace
preconditions: A workspace with studies, raw objects, reports, audit history and interrupted jobs; a consistent backup and a different supported storage location
actions: Create and verify a whole-workspace backup
Restore into an authorized destination and reconcile interrupted operations
Open historical studies and reproduce a selected report
Review deployment, storage and device readiness
acceptance: The backup covers a consistent database/object snapshot with integrity manifests, audit and pending-operation state; a design-only export is never represented as a data backup
Relocation resolves internal object references without requiring old absolute paths and does not accidentally bind another workspace object
Corrupt or missing objects produce a repairable restore state rather than a false successful restoration
Interrupted jobs and staged promotions reconcile without duplicate artifacts or stale success
Restoring never automatically reopens live participant endpoints, pairs devices or resumes capture; deployment authorization and readiness are reviewed separately
Historical cohorts, raw inputs and report hashes remain traceable after restore
evidence: Consistent database/object and selected report hashes

journeys.name: Withdraw or purge retained data without confusing archive
journeys.actor: Authorized researcher handling a participant request or retention policy
preconditions: A participant with recordings, derivatives, cached artifacts, report contributions and backups under an explicit withdrawal/retention policy
actions: Inspect affected records and the permitted retention action
Apply authorized removal or restriction
Review downstream report and cache consequences
Restore a backup under the recorded deletion policy
Archive and restore an unrelated study
acceptance: Archive changes organization/read-only policy and never implies deletion, anonymization or withdrawal completion
The action enumerates raw records, derivatives, caches, indexes, shared references, report contributions and backups within its authorized scope
Deletion/restriction tombstones contain the minimum necessary identifiers and policy/audit evidence rather than the removed participant content
Where purge is required, old backups follow the declared expiry/cryptographic erasure or restore-suppression policy; restoration replays tombstones before researcher or participant access
Report provenance records removal/redaction or required reanalysis; missing observations never become zero scores and frozen copies are not silently falsified

Objects still legitimately referenced elsewhere follow scope and retention policy rather than indiscriminate byte deletion; irretrievable external downloads remain distinguishable from controlled storage
